questions.question: A cyclist travels at a constant speed of 18 km/h. How long will it take to cover a distance of 45 km?
questions.explanation: Time = distance ÷ speed = 45 km ÷ 18 km/h = 2.5 h. The cyclist needs two and a half hours to travel 45 km.

questions.question: A train travels 150 miles in 3 hours. If it continues at the same speed, how far will it travel in 5.5 hours?
questions.explanation: First find speed: 150 mi ÷ 3 h = 50 mi/h. Then distance for 5.5 h = 50 mi/h × 5.5 h = 275 miles.

questions.question: A runner completes a 10 km race in 42 minutes. What is the runner's average speed in meters per second (m/s)?
questions.explanation: Convert distance to meters: 10 km = 10,000 m. Convert time to seconds: 42 min = 42 × 60 = 2520 s. Speed = 10,000 m ÷ 2520 s ≈ 3.97 m/s.
